name: Sonnet macro/sector rotation
strategy: Catalyst-driven sector rotation into healthcare/biotech and regional banks funded by shorting exhausted semis/AI-capex and weak discretionary momentum, with a crypto momentum-breakdown short overlay.

positions.thesis: Weekly move is flat (+0.03%) but the quarter has quietly built to +16.73%, the second-best quarter-level read in the book; sized up modestly from 8% to 9% to lean into the medium-term catalyst-optionality trend, keeping the wide -15%/+35% stop/TP.

Healthcare re-rating has reaccelerated after last week's cooling read — +1.02% this week and +14.14% over the quarter confirm the trend is intact, not just a one-month artifact; sized up from 14% to 15%.
Financials rotation remains the steadiest core long (+0.97% wk, +13.39% qtr); held flat at 15%, still the largest single-conviction position in the book.
Regional banks put in the strongest weekly print in the book (+2.26%), the clearest confirmation yet that the financials rotation is broadening beyond the majors; sized up from 10% to 12%.
Low-vol ballast trimmed slightly from 6% to 5% to help fund the higher-conviction longs; still a small defensive sleeve, no new signal either way.

Discretionary laggard thesis, which had stalled to flat and got trimmed to 7% last week, is reconfirming with a -1.38% weekly decline — the first real down-week since the trim; sized back up to 8%, keeping the -12%/+25% stop/TP.

6-month momentum-breakdown thesis (-37.7% 6mo) remains unrefuted even as the near-term read is flat-to-slightly-positive (-0.10% wk, +1.2% mo); held flat at 5% with the wide -40% stop, no funding cost to stay patient on a short.

reassessment_note: Weekly desk 2026-08-15: Sized up the confirming healthcare/biotech/regional-bank longs (XLV, KRE, XBI) on stronger weekly and quarterly reads, trimmed SPLV ballast slightly to fund them, and reactivated the XLY discretionary short on its first real down-week (-1.38%) since last week's trim to flat momentum. Held off reinstating a semis/AI-capex short despite the mandate's short leg: SMH's weekly move has cooled sharply from the +12.99% squeeze that forced this book to cover SMH last week to a much calmer +0.88% this week, but it's still a positive week, and this exact trade type has caused 12 of 17 standing-order stop-outs platform-wide historically — waiting for an actual down-week before re-shorting rather than re-risking into a still-positive tape. SOL-USD short held flat; its 6-month momentum-breakdown thesis (-37.7%) remains unrefuted even though the near-term read is flat-to-slightly-positive.
novelty: Zero symbol overlap with the Round 2 book (healthcare/financials/biotech longs plus a discretionary/crypto short overlay here, versus small-cap/industrial/gold/EM/duration longs there) — 0% same-direction gross-weight overlap, well under the 50% cap.
research_notes:
Read the account packet (NAV, positions, stops, entered 2026-08-10) for both books. WebSearch was exhausted for the session, so pulled fresh Perf Week/Month/Quarter data via WebFetch on finviz.com for every held symbol (GLD, IWM, SMH, XLF, XLV, XLI, TLT, FXI, XBI, KRE, SPLV, XLY) plus current price/return context for GLD/IWM/SMH/XLF/XLV via stockanalysis.com, and SOL price/7d/30d change via coingecko.com, all as of the 2026-08-14 close.

Key findings: (1) GLD's momentum decelerated hard, from last week's +13.76% GDX/+3.46% gold squeeze to just +0.76% this week (month still +10.01%) — a real change from the "accelerating" read used to size it up last week. (2) FXI had its worst week since entry (-3.54%), reversing the "stalled but not reversing" read from last week and pulling it toward its -8% stop. (3) TLT has now lost money for three straight months (-0.87% wk/-2.58% mo/-3.39% qtr) — the Fed-cut duration hedge isn't being confirmed by price action, yields are grinding higher not lower. (4) IWM is the cleanest confirming trade in the R2 book across all three timeframes (+1.17% wk/+3.21% mo/+7.26% qtr). (5) SMH's squeeze has cooled sharply (+12.99% wk last week to +0.88% wk now, quarter only +1.64%, weakest quarter read in the R3 book), suggesting the "exhausted" AI-infra thesis may be re-approaching viability, but it's still a positive week and this desk has a specific history of stop-outs on this exact short — chose to wait for an actual down-week rather than re-risk immediately. (6) KRE posted the strongest weekly print in either book (+2.26%), confirming regional-bank breadth beyond the majors. (7) XLV and XBI both show strong quarter-level reads (+14.14%, +16.73%) reaccelerating after a cooling month. (8) XLY's short thesis reconfirmed with its first real down-week (-1.38%) since being trimmed last week on a flat month. (9) SOL-USD is flat/slightly positive near-term but the 6-month breakdown (-37.7%) is intact, no reason to change a no-funding-cost short.

Result: rebalanced both books — de-risked R2's two hottest/most-decelerating legs (GLD, FXI) plus the unconfirmed TLT hedge into more cash (43%→52%), while sizing up R2's cleanest confirming trade (IWM); sized up R3's confirming longs (XLV, KRE, XBI) and reactivated the XLY short, held SOL-USD short flat, and deliberately did not reinstate a semis/AI-capex short given the stop-out history and still-positive (if cooling) SMH tape. R2 and R3 books have zero symbol overlap, so the <50% overlap constraint is trivially satisfied.
